name: jungle_depths_mapstyle_a
prompt:
16-bit pixel art style-selection sheet for a top-down bomberman-style JUNGLE DEPTHS stage. Exactly 4 separate mini-map panels arranged in a neat 2x2 grid on one flat plain cream background (#F7F1E3). Each panel is ONE complete 10x10 tile map, seen from directly above like a board-game board, at the same scale and camera, each panel occupying one equal quarter of the image with a generous empty margin, nothing crossing between panels. No labels, no text, no numbers, no watermark, no UI, no frames, no grid lines between panels, no characters, no drop shadows, no floor plane outside each map. Every map is a dense jungle ruin interior: enclosed on all four sides by non-walkable wall props, with a readable network of open floor paths, 6-10 destructible blocks in small clusters, and exactly one multi-tile structure (3x2 tiles) per map. All tiles align to an invisible square grid. Crisp hand-placed pixels, true pixel art, 1px selective dark outline, flat cel shading with 2-3 tones, top-left light, saturated but earthy palette, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft gradient.

TOP-LEFT PANEL - MOSSY STONE RUIN (grey-green, damp, cold light): floor of seamless mossy grey stone slabs in 2 variants with 1px dark grout and green moss in the cracks; wall props are broken moss-covered pillars, fern clumps, a cracked ancient stone idol head sunk into the ground; destructible blocks are chipped mossy stone cubes, and ONE of them is pale green with a carved snake-scale diamond relief as a small accent; the 3x2 structure is an overgrown stone arch gate with a tiny carved serpent above the lintel.

TOP-RIGHT PANEL - ROOT HOLLOW (rich leaf green, dark soil brown, humid shadow): floor of packed earth and leaf litter with moss patches and scattered fallen leaves; wall props are massive tree roots, cut tree stumps with growth rings, dense fern bushes, one stump carved with a coiled snake as a small accent; destructible blocks are mossy log-crates with bark texture, one painted with a simple serpent coil; the 3x2 structure is a huge hollow tree-trunk arch with roots spreading over the ground.

BOTTOM-LEFT PANEL - SERPENT TEMPLE (warm sandstone, jade green, aged gold, torch warmth): floor of warm sandstone tiles with a subtle geometric inlay border; wall props are a carved serpent-head stone pillar, a jade brazier, vine-wrapped stone blocks; destructible blocks are sandstone cubes with a shallow gold snake relief and jade cubes, snake motif only on a few blocks; the 3x2 structure is a temple gate flanked by two facing stone serpents.

BOTTOM-RIGHT PANEL - GLOW SWAMP (deep teal, blue-green, bioluminescent cyan): floor of wet dark teal mud and shallow reflective water pools with glowing spore dots; wall props are clusters of glowing turquoise mushrooms, twisted mangrove roots, a half-sunken snake skeleton idol as a small accent; destructible blocks are wet dark stone cubes and translucent turquoise snake-scale cubes that emit a faint pixel glow; the 3x2 structure is a sunken serpent statue rising from the water.

RULES: snake-themed elements appear only as a MINOR accent (one brick type, one wall prop, one structure at most) in each map; the main theme stays jungle/forest depths. All four maps share the same tile scale, same outline weight, same top-left light and same level of detail. Tiny readable props, clean silhouettes, every walkable cell clearly different from every blocking cell.
